subject.title: [Feature]: Add tools.web.fetch.allowPrivateNetwork to allow private network access

question: Should OpenClaw expose private-network access for `web_fetch`, and if so should it be broad global config or a narrower audited per-agent/hostname-scoped SSRF policy?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but allowing arbitrary `web_fetch` to reach private/internal networks changes a security boundary and repository policy requires maintainer intent for new config/security surfaces.

options.title: Approve narrow audited policy
options.body: Continue through a per-agent or hostname-scoped design with audit output, cache isolation, and explicit authorization semantics before merging.

options.title: Approve broad global opt-in
options.body: Expose a global dangerous flag only if maintainers intentionally accept the wider blast radius and document metadata, redirect, and operator-risk boundaries.

options.title: Decline broad private access
options.body: Keep arbitrary `web_fetch` strict and route remaining needs through fake-IP proxy flags, provider-specific trusted origins, or the broader egress-control issue.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow audited policy
recommendation.body: Continue through a per-agent or hostname-scoped design with audit output, cache isolation, and explicit authorization semantics before merging.

likelyOwner.reason: He has direct issue-thread context on this exact security-sensitive config decision and relevant SSRF/web-tools history.
